study: studies/identifiability/ecpe-positive-control/ecpe_control.py (literature rank 11: latent-level positive control on ECPE)
note: A LIKELIHOOD-BASED LATENT TEST SEES THE PUBLISHED ECPE HIERARCHY; NONE OF THE PROGRAMME'S CROSS-SECTIONAL INSTRUMENTS CAN. Reference: saturated DCM (saturated LCDM / G-DINA, EM in numpy) against the hierarchical model for lexical -> cohesive -> morphosyntactic (Templin & Bradshaw 2014; order from a secondary source), parametric-bootstrap LRT (Ma & Xu 2021), 2,922 examinees x 28 items. Floor passes: size 0/60, power 40/40 at forbidden mass 0.10, reversed-chain power 60/60. Real: HIERARCHY FOUND, narrowly -- H_PUB LR 25.51, p = 0.068 (B = 500; Monte Carlo interval [0.046, 0.091] straddles 0.05); H_REV and the other four linear orders all p = 0.002 (LR 94-427). IITA against fixed margins (skill grain), IITA-PAIRSCAN (item grain) and the conjunctive interaction test (skill grain) all FAIL their ECPE-shaped floors (recover the planted hierarchy in 0.02, 0.25 and 0.245 of replicates; the interaction reading is as common in the reversed world, 0.24), so each is UNANSWERABLE: a detection-floor statement on a corpus with a known reference. On ECPE's attribute correlation a one-trait threshold model is itself a linear hierarchy (forbidden mass 2e-14), so a test that holds one trait cannot see it. Drop and lag cannot run on cross-sectional data. A4 (positive control, real material) is not moved: the known structure was recovered only by the external reference, not by the assay. Moves nothing.
